Subject: Pricing trigger matrix and reseller split — follow-up

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is pulling together the PO and we have two quick questions before we move to signatures:

1) The pricing sheet we received references a "threshold trigger matrix" that moves us from a committed rate to a true-up rate if monthly consumption falls below X for two consecutive months. Can you confirm the exact cadence and whether the true-up is pro-rated?

2) We will be onboarding through a reseller partner (HealthCloud Resellers). How should we represent the channel margin in the PO? We need to show the net amount Redwood receives and the reseller pass-through amount for our finance team. Our reseller has asked for a 17% margin — is that supported under the private offer?

I'm attaching our standard PO template so we can iterate. If you prefer, we can jump on a 20-minute call.

Subject: Re: Pricing trigger matrix and reseller split — follow-up

Hi Susan — great to hear from you and thanks for the PO template. Quick answers below, and I copied Ben (channel ops) to make sure the reseller split is fully covered.

1) Trigger cadence: our standard private-offer trigger checks a 30-day rolling windows and evaluates a two-month consecutive shortfall before converting back to the true-up rate. The true-up is pro-rated to the shortfall in the billing period; we apply it to the next invoice as an adjustment line. I attached the trigger matrix (v2) for clarity — it shows example scenarios and how adjustments appear on invoices.

2) Reseller margin: we support including a reseller pass-through line on the PO. Net pricing to Redwood should be the "Net Vendor Amount" field in the template. For a 17% reseller margin, we typically model that as an explicit reseller fee line so your finance team can see gross vs net. That said, there are a couple of constraints: resellers taking >20% margin sometimes require an approval for certain SKUs, and for meter-based SKUs we ask that the reseller fee be static (percentage or flat) rather than dynamically tiered — it simplifies reconciliation.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm whether KiteHealth's proposed 17% margin is acceptable for the Azure private-offer SKUs and if any approvals are required? Also, Ben — please review the attached matrix and flag any SKU exclusions.

If helpful I can schedule a short call with our channel team and your procurement.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of GTM Strategy — Marketplaces, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pricing trigger matrix and reseller split — follow-up

Thanks Naomi — adding my channel ops perspective.

Hi Susan — quick practicals from the partner/ops side:
- 17% reseller margin: acceptable for list/flat-fee SKUs. For metered/usage SKUs we recommend capping reseller margin at 15% unless the reseller can provide monthly reporting that maps to our meter (we've seen reconciliation drift otherwise).
- Approval path: 17% doesn't require leadership sign-off for Azure/GCP private offers, but we will need a short note in the contract appendix that the reseller margin is a pass-through (we'll help with language).
- Invoice treatment: Redwood can appear as the vendor of record with an explicit reseller distribution line. KiteHealth's PO can use the template Naomi sent; we will return an invoice showing the Net Vendor Amount and the Reseller Fee as separate lines.

Jordan — on SKU exclusions: please review the matrix for the following SKUs we flag as "no-reseller-pass": RH-EMBED-XL and RH-OPT-LOW-LATENCY (these require additional infra/entitlements). Jordan, can you confirm any other SKUs?

Susan — if you're ok, I'll prepare an annotated PO that maps to the matrix and includes an example invoice row for both committed and true-up cases. That should make your finance sign-off faster.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
